subject: Dedicated capacity sizing call - scheduling & prep
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@shoply.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@shoply.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing call - scheduling & prep

Hi Olivia / Samir —

Thanks again for the discovery call today — great context on Shoply's search personalization project. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can get the right folks on a technical sizing call for Dedicated: 

Summary notes (from today's call):
- Primary workload: realtime personalization & re-ranking for product search results.
- Peak traffic: expected to be in short bursts around promotion windows; rough estimate you gave: 80–120 requests/sec peak.
- Typical request size: ~100–150 tokens (prompt + context).
- Target latency: p95 target ideally <300ms for generation latency (end-to-end SLO will include routing and deserialization).
- Data concerns: VPC + SOC2 scope, no persistent sharing of PII.

What I'd like to schedule: a 60-min Dedicated capacity sizing call / technical deep dive with our infra lead (Michael) and solutions engineer (Dev) to go over: exact qps targets, traffic shaping, batching behavior, KV cache usage, model family you expect to run, and any compliance/network constraints. We'll also review a recommended capacity profile and pricing for reserved pools.

Proposed times (PT):
- Tue Aug 10, 10:00–11:00am
- Tue Aug 10, 2:00–3:00pm
- Wed Aug 11, 11:00–12:00pm

If none of those work, tell me a couple windows and we'll adapt. I've attached a short sizing template (redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx) — if you can pre-fill approximate qps by endpoint and avg tokens, it will speed the call.

Thanks — looking forward to taking this live.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@shoply.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@shoply.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing call - scheduling & prep

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches our notes. We definitely want a technical deep dive with Michael and Dev.

Availability on our side:
- Tue Aug 10, 2:00–3:00pm PT works best (Samir and I are available)
- If you need earlier, Wed Aug 11 11:00–12:00pm PT is also possible.

A few additional details to help prep:
- Primary model: open-source re-ranking model (we're testing both gpt-like rerankers and a smaller transformer); we'll confirm exact model family on Tuesday but expect sequence lengths in the 120–180 token range.
- Expected burst behavior: we have promotional spikes where QPS can jump ~2–3x for 2–5 minutes. Average daily QPS is lower.
- Compliance: VPC + SOC2 required; we have a procurement checklist to share after the sizing call.

I've attached a quick capacity sheet with our initial estimates (capacity_req_sheet.xlsx). Samir will join the call and can share more details on infra constraints.

See you Tue 2pm PT if that works on your side.

Cheers,
Olivia Chen
Director, Search & Personalization
Shoply, Inc.
olivia.chen@shoply.com

Attachment: capacity_req_sheet.xlsx

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@shoply.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing call - scheduling & prep

Great — thanks Olivia. I'm confirming on our side that Tue Aug 10 2:00–3:00pm PT is reserved. I've created a calendar invite (link below) and included Michael for kernel/runtime questions.

Pre-call ask (helps us scope the recommended Dedicated config):
- Can you confirm per-endpoint peak qps (search, rerank, personalization) if you have them split? If not, total peak qps is fine.
- Typical prompt / response token breakdown (prompt vs model output).
- Are you planning to use KV cache / session caching or stateless prompt calls?
- Required p95 latency SLOs and whether tail latency >300ms would be acceptable for small batch windows.

We'll bring:
- An initial capacity profile (GPU type, # of instances, estimated sustained vs burst throughput)
- Options for autoscaling/burst capacity and canary rollout plan
- A short checklist for network/VPC peering and SOC2 evidence items to speed procurement

Calendar invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=shoply-capacity-call-20260810
Redwood prep doc (view): https://drive.redwood.ai/sizing-templates/Shoply-prep

Looking forward to the call.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-sla.pdf

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@shoply.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@shoply.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing call - scheduling & prep

Perfect — thanks Dev. Confirming Tue Aug 10, 2:00–3:00pm PT. Samir and I will join. A couple quick clarifications before the meeting:

- Peak split: rough split is 70% search queries (lighter prompts, ~80–100 tokens) and 30% rerank requests (heavier, ~140–180 tokens). Total peak ~110 qps.
- We do use a short-lived KV cache for session context on re-rank flows (not full long-term caching).
- p95 latency target: <300ms preferred. We can accept short-lived tail latency up to ~500ms during promotional bursts if autoscaling catches up.
- We'll upload a filled version of the sizing template to the Drive link you shared before the call.

See you both at 2pm PT.

Best,
Olivia
